statement: Lower Salmon 4-Day maximum is 30 total people (5 guides and 25 guests).
Main Salmon 5-Day (or 4-Day high-water variant) maximum is 30 total people (5 guides and 25 guests).
Jetboat shuttle maximum is 24 guests.

Lower Salmon requires a shuttle driver to drop guides boats and gear at Hammer Creek launch; the driver returns the van and trailer; a driver van and trailer must pick up at Heller Bar on the afternoon of day 4.

Main Salmon requires a driver van and trailer to drop at Corn Creek (approximately 10 hours from launch); the crew camps overnight; trip starts 9 am the following morning; the driver returns the van/trailer to Riggins after launch.
Typical full multi-day boat mix is 2 large gear boats and 3 paddle boats; smaller groups may run fewer paddle boats or a Mammoth but always require at least one gear boat.
Buses require a CDL-qualified driver.
Maximum one full-day trip per day.
Maximum two half-day trips per day (10 am and 2 pm).
Main Salmon has assigned launch dates.
Lower Salmon preferred launch days are Monday and Tuesday; other days permitted when needed.
Day-trip and French Creek maximum combined volume is 120 people.
One seat and one PFD required per guest.
Each multi-day trip requires one lead guide (typically 2-3 years experience).
Day-trip paddle boats limited to 9 guests on a 16-ft boat.
French Creek / SRHAB paddle boats limited to 10 guests on a 16-ft boat.
A guide may be assigned to only one boat at a time on the same trip.
Ruby (old van) must not tow.
Buses must not travel to Vinegar (French Creek / SRHAB launch).
French Creek / SRHAB requires multiple drivers and vehicles (typically one van + mega trailer plus another van; larger trips need two vans and two trailers) for both drop and pickup.
One person must work the store each working day.
Two oars required for each boat.
One paddle required for each person in a paddle boat.
Helmets required during high water; helmets always required in inflatable kayaks or on scout rafting trips.
First-aid kit required on each trip.
Each raft requires a perimeter-line rope.
Thwarts/seats must be set for the correct passenger count; boats must be properly inflated.
Each trip requires a pump.
Safety talk required before every trip.
One throw rope required per boat.
Main Salmon and Middle Fork permits and camps must be submitted at least two weeks before launch.
Other rivers (BLM) report usage only at end of season.
Two half-days on the same day (Hagerman or Riggins) are a hard limit.
A guide must not be sent alone on Murtaugh multi-day trips or any high-water trip; solo is permitted on low-water Hagerman and on Riggins full-day and half-day trips.
Day-trip paddle boats each require 4 straps.
Frame straps required at 4 per boat (6 for big boats).
Spare PFDs required at 1 per 15 people.
One invasive-species sticker required per boat.
SRHAB / French Creek requires one boat pump for every 4 boats.
A guide with an approved Blackout request or Assignment block on a trip date cannot be assigned that day.
Store Staff cannot also hold a guide driver or food role on the same day.
A guide assigned to a multi-day trip cannot take any other overlapping assignment for the duration of that trip.
The same vehicle or trailer cannot be assigned to two same-launch-day operations unless cleared by stacking shuttle-pool or rig-group rules.
A jetboat trip type (Lower Salmon 4-Day or Main Salmon 4-Day) on a today-or-future date must have Jetboat confirmed checked.
Main Salmon and Middle Fork trips are hard-capped at 25 guests and 5 guides.
A trip that has boats to haul (Total boats > 0) must have a trailer assigned when a van/driver is present.
Boats on a trip may not exceed the assigned trailer’s Boat capacity (standard = 5 mega = 10).
A rental operation’s assigned vehicle or trailer is blocked for the full rental span and cannot be assigned elsewhere on intervening days.
Each vehicle assigned to a movement must have its own driver.
A CDL-required vehicle must be driven by a CDL-qualified driver.
A guide assigned to a trip whose date falls before their Season start date or after their Season end date is invalid.
A driver whose Drivers License Expiration has passed or whose CDL/DOT medical has expired cannot be assigned.
A vehicle on manual hold or with an open critical issue cannot be assigned to a trip.
Movement drivers are subject to the same time-off blackout and season rules as Daily Op crew.
A Middle Fork trip with no Shuttle details is invalid.
A Main Salmon Lower Salmon or Overnighter trip with Guest shuttle coordinated unchecked is invalid when inside the hard window.
For Full Day Half Day Overnighter or SRHAB day-3 operations 1–11 people require 1 van.
For Full Day Half Day Overnighter or SRHAB day-3 operations 12–23 people require 2 vans.
For Full Day Half Day Overnighter or SRHAB day-3 operations 24–25 people require 3 vans.
For Full Day Half Day Overnighter or SRHAB day-3 operations 26–36 people require 3 vans or 1 bus.
For Full Day Half Day Overnighter or SRHAB day-3 operations 37 or more people require a bus.
Standard day-trip 16-ft boats are limited to 9 guests; SRHAB / French Creek 16-ft boats are limited to 10 guests.

Designated lead for a multi-day section must be one of the 2026 named leads for that section (Abigail Brown for Middle Fork Connor P or Ammon for Lower Hannah or Eric Newell for Main Logan for French/SRHAB).
Soft capacity warning fires when boats exceed the comfortable load of 4 on a standard trailer or 8 on a Mega trailer.
A driver on big drives three consecutive days triggers a soft fatigue flag on the third day.
A guide or driver finishing a movement needs at least 180 minutes before starting a day-trip assignment; shorter gaps are a soft tight-turnaround flag.
When a Vehicle record has no Passenger seats value the default seat count used for capacity checks is 15.
A pickup movement with 25 or more riders and no bus assigned triggers a soft “bus likely needed” flag.
Two jobs on the same rig are clear if the gap between their time windows is at least 60 minutes; a smaller gap with no overlap is a soft tight-turnaround flag; real overlap is hard.
A movement carrying people with no vehicle assigned is hard within 1 day of the trip soft within 3 days and silent further out.
“Bus driver not confirmed” only flags within 4 days of the trip.
Guest-shuttle-not-coordinated with no details is hard within 2 days of the trip and soft further out.
A Riggins day-trip operation with zero guests is treated as not running; its movements do not commit rigs or crew.
Middle Fork trips are exempt from the per-movement passenger-seat capacity check.
A CDL-required vehicle must be driven by a CDL-qualified driver.
Store Staff cannot also hold a guide driver or food role on the same day.
